item.title: Hardware-backed GPG (YubiKey)
item.description:
Table of Contents

  • What a YubiKey actually does (not what people think)
  • Why this matters (and why software keys are weak)
  • What you actually need
  • Install the required junk (once)
  • Reset the OpenPGP app (clean slate)
  • Generate keys on the hardware, not on disk
  • Verify the key is actually hardware-backed
  • Force touch confirmation (non-negotiable)
  • Use it with Git (the only reason most people care)
  • Add the public key to GitHub
  • Backups (because hardware breaks)
  • What this setup protects you from
  • The takeaway

Most people using GPG are doing it wrong. If your private key exists on your disk, you’ve already lost the point. Malware, backups, cloud sync, laptop theft — take your pick. Hardware-backed GPG fixes this by doing something radical:

Supply-chain attack = Compromising trust, not code. Attackers don’t “hack users”. They become someone you already trust.

item.title: Why Git still uses ancient auth
item.description:
Table of Contents

  • 1. Git was designed for a hostile, disconnected world
  • 2. Git does NOT authenticate users — transports do
  • 3. Git’s data model predates “accounts”
  • 4. Changing auth would break the ecosystem
  • 5. Git optimizes for verification, not permission
  • 6. Central platforms had to adapt to Git — not vice versa
  • 7. Why this feels painful today
  • 💡 The uncomfortable truth
  • TL;DR (burn this in)
    • One-liner to remember
